content.title: Relationships Among Chords, Secants, and Tangents
content.overview: This lesson focuses on the geometric relationships and segment lengths created when secants and tangents intersect at a point outside a circle. By applying the External-Product Match strategy, you can solve for unknown lengths using the properties of external segments and whole secant lengths.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between external secant segments and whole secant lengths.
Apply the Secant-Secant Theorem to find missing segment lengths.
Apply the Tangent-Secant Theorem to calculate tangent or secant lengths.
Verify solutions by comparing calculated values against ACT multiple-choice options.

sections.title: Key Definitions
sections.content: A secant is a line that intersects a circle at two points. When a secant is drawn from an external point P, it creates two segments: the external segment (the distance from P to the first intersection point) and the internal chord (the segment inside the circle). The whole secant length is the sum of the external segment and the internal chord. A tangent is a line that touches the circle at exactly one point.

sections.title: The Secant-Secant Theorem
sections.content: When two secants intersect at a point outside a circle, the product of the external segment and the whole length of the first secant is equal to the product of the external segment and the whole length of the second secant. Formula: (External 1) × (Whole 1) = (External 2) × (Whole 2).

sections.title: The Tangent-Secant Theorem
sections.content:
When a tangent and a secant intersect at a point outside a circle, the square of the tangent segment's length is equal to the product of the external secant segment and the whole secant length. Formula: (Tangent)^2 = (External Secant) × (Whole Secant).

![A flowchart showing the steps to solve for secant and tangent segments: Identify External/Whole, Multiply External by Whole, Set Equation, Solve.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0ee6e3df-821b-4f7f-b4f0-cbf6d2708536-1786506024285-550.webp)

worked_examples.question: Point P is outside circle O. A secant from P meets the circle at A and B so that the external segment PA = 3 and the internal chord AB = 5. A tangent from P touches the circle at T. What is the length of tangent PT?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the segments. The external secant segment PA = 3. The internal chord AB = 5. Step 2: Calculate the whole secant length. Whole = PA + AB = 3 + 5 = 8. Step 3: Apply the Tangent-Secant Theorem. PT^2 = (External) × (Whole) = 3 × 8 = 24. Step 4: Solve for PT. PT = √24. Simplify the radical: √24 = √(4 × 6) = 2√6. The length of PT is 2√6.

worked_examples.question: Two secants are drawn from point P to a circle. The first secant has an external segment of 4 and an internal chord of 6. The second secant has an external segment of 5 and an unknown internal chord x. Find the value of x.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Calculate the whole length of the first secant. Whole 1 = 4 + 6 = 10. Step 2: Express the whole length of the second secant. Whole 2 = 5 + x. Step 3: Apply the Secant-Secant Theorem. (External 1) × (Whole 1) = (External 2) × (Whole 2) -> 4 × 10 = 5 × (5 + x). Step 4: Solve for x. 40 = 25 + 5x -> 15 = 5x -> x = 3.

common_mistakes: Using the internal chord length instead of the whole secant length in the product formula.
Forgetting to square the tangent length when using the Tangent-Secant Theorem.
Adding the segments for the final calculation instead of multiplying them (External × Whole).
exam_tips: Always draw a diagram and label the 'External' and 'Whole' parts clearly before setting up your equation.
If a result is a radical like √24, use your calculator to find the decimal (≈ 4.9) to quickly eliminate whole-number distractors.
content.recap: To solve circle segment problems involving an external point, remember the 'External-Product Match': multiply the external segment by the whole secant length. For tangents, square the tangent length and set it equal to that product.

knowledge_claims.content: The external secant segment is the distance from the external intersection point to the nearest point on the circle's circumference.
The whole secant length is calculated by adding the external segment length to the length of the internal chord.
The Secant-Secant Theorem states that (External 1) × (Whole 1) = (External 2) × (Whole 2) for two secants meeting at an external point.
The Tangent-Secant Theorem states that the square of the tangent length equals the product of the external secant segment and the whole secant length.
A common error is multiplying the external segment by only the internal chord rather than the whole secant length.
The relationship for a tangent (t), external secant (e), and internal chord (i) is expressed as t^2 = e(e + i).
The External-Product Match strategy is triggered when a diagram shows a tangent or secants intersecting at a point outside the circle.
After calculating a radical length for a tangent, approximating the decimal value helps verify the answer against ACT choices.
In the context of these theorems, a tangent segment is treated as having its external segment and whole length be identical, which is why it is squared.
If a secant has an external segment of 3 and an internal chord of 5, the value used in the product formula is 3 × 8.
To find an unknown internal chord length using the Secant-Secant Theorem, set up the equation (E1)(W1) = (E2)(E2 + x) and solve for x.
Unlike central angles which relate to arcs, secant and tangent theorems relate specifically to the linear lengths of line segments.

videoLesson.title: Compute External-Whole Segment Products
videoLesson.description: Identify external and whole secant lengths in the diagram as concrete variables. Multiply external×whole for each secant and set tangent^2 equal to that product.
